To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CSI MG method, when coupled with the vorticity streamfunction formulation of the two-dimensional NavierStokes flow equations, is an effective tool for the numerical determination of high Re solutions.

the coupled strongly implicit (CSI) MG algorithm is a powerful method for the solution of the vorticity streamfunction formulation of the two-dimensional incompressible Navie-Stokes equations for high Reynolds number flows.

(1) the coupled strongly implicit (CSI) multigrid method can be used to solve efficiently the two dimensional in compressible NavierStrokes equations in a rectangular domain for high Reynolds number flows, and (2) the use of the CSI MG method for solving the NavierStokes equation in the vorticity stream-function form is computationally more efficient than its use in the velocity-pressure form.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the CSI-MG method for solving numerically the NavierStokes equation on a series of uniform mesh grids.
the development and testing of the CSI MG method for the numerical solution of high Re incompressible flow problems.
the development of a numerical technique for solving the two dimensional in compressible flow problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CSI MG method is a powerful and efficient numerical tool for the solution of the vorticity stream-function formulation of the incompressible Naviers tokes equations.
the coupled strongly implicit MG method has proven to be a very effective technique for the solution of the Navier Stokes equation.
the CSI MG method is a very powerful and robust method for the numerical solution of the vorticity streamfunction formulation of the two-dimensional incompressible Naviers-Stokes equations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a coupled multigrid technique which can be used to solve efficiently the NavierStokes equation for high Reynolds number flow problems on fine meshes.
the coupled strongly implicit (CSI) MG method is very promising and effective.
the MG method is a viable and efficient tool for the solution of the two dimensional, incompressible, NavierStokes equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MG technique is an effective tool for enhancing the convergence of iterative methods for solving discretization equations of the NavierStokes and other governing equations.
the coupled strongly implicit multi-grid method can be used to obtain high Re fine mesh solutions of the incompressible NaviersStokes equations.
a multigrid approach to solving the Navier-Stokes equations is a promising technique for obtaining solutions to the driven cavity problem.
